elements.content: Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: a formal idea or set of ideas intended to explain something.
items.example: Scientists are re-examining a 42-year-old childhood obesity theory.

items.definition: the chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.
items.example: Basal metabolism accounts for most daily energy expenditure.

items.definition: a proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence.
items.example: The initial hypothesis was disproved by modern metabolic tracking.

items.definition: the action of spending or using up energy.
items.example: Daily energy expenditure varies significantly across age groups.

items.definition: a mutual relationship or connection between two or more things.
items.example: A statistical correlation does not prove a direct causal link.

items.definition: the fact or condition of being widespread.
items.example: The prevalence of childhood health conditions prompted extensive research.

items.definition: relating to heat or energy value of food.
items.example: Caloric balance depends on both diet and physical activity.

items.definition: the process of assessing something again.
items.example: Scientific progress relies on constant re-evaluation of old models.

items.definition: tending to spend much time seated; somewhat inactive.
items.example: A sedentary lifestyle contributes to energy imbalance.

items.definition: involving information about the same subjects over a long period of time.
items.example: Longitudinal studies provide robust evidence across decades.

elements.title: Grammar Explanation (Upper-Intermediate (B2))
elements.content:
Use modal + have + past participle to speculate about past scientific assumptions (e.g., Earlier researchers might have overlooked key metabolic variables).

elements.title: Key Study Insights & Core Takeaways
elements.text: Researchers conducted in-depth investigations and empirical trials to analyze these phenomena. The findings reveal critical mechanisms that challenge earlier assumptions.
elements.takeaway: Understanding both biological and empirical evidence allows us to draw more grounded conclusions.
